subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As a general rule, CGST and SGST/UTGST are levied on all intra-State supplies of goods and/or services, while IGST is levied on all inter-State supplies, based on:

options.B: Whether the location of the supplier and the place of supply of goods or services are in the same State/UT (intra-State) or in different States/UTs (inter-State)
options.A: Whether the supplier is a company or an individual
options.C: Whether the recipient is registered or unregistered under GST
options.D: Whether the value of supply exceeds fifty lakh rupees

answer_html:
Correct answer: (B) Whether the location of the supplier and the place of supply of goods or services are in the same State/UT (intra-State) or in different States/UTs (inter-State)

As a general rule, where the location of the supplier and the place of supply of goods or services are in the same State/Union Territory, it is treated as an intra-State supply; where they are in different States/UTs, it is treated as an inter-State supply. CGST and SGST/UTGST are levied on intra-State supplies, while IGST is levied on inter-State supplies.

question_html: As per section 2(6), "aggregate turnover" means the aggregate value of all taxable supplies (excluding inward supplies on which tax is payable on reverse charge basis), exempt supplies, exports and inter-State supplies of persons having the same PAN, computed:

options.C: On an all-India basis, but excluding central tax, State tax, Union territory tax, integrated tax and cess

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As per section 2(45), "Electronic Commerce Operator" means:

options.D: Any person who owns, operates or manages a digital or electronic facility or platform for electronic commerce
options.A: Any person who supplies goods or services exclusively through a physical retail store
options.B: Only a person who is registered as a company under the Companies Act, 2013 and sells goods online
options.C: Any person who merely advertises goods or services on a website without facilitating any transaction

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) Any person who owns, operates or manages a digital or electronic facility or platform for electronic commerce

As per section 2(45), "Electronic Commerce Operator" means any person who owns, operates or manages a digital or electronic facility or platform for electronic commerce. "Electronic Commerce" itself, per section 2(44), means the supply of goods or services or both, including digital products, over digital or electronic networks.

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As per section 2(47), "exempt supply" means supply of any goods or services or both which attracts nil rate of tax, or which is wholly exempt under section 11 (or section 6 of the IGST Act), and additionally includes:

options.A: Non-taxable supply
options.B: Only zero-rated supply, and no other category
options.C: Only supplies made to the Government, and no other category
options.D: Composite supply only, to the exclusion of mixed supply

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Non-taxable supply

As per section 2(47), "exempt supply" means supply of any goods or services or both which attracts nil rate of tax or which may be wholly exempt from tax under section 11 (or under section 6 of the IGST Act), and includes non-taxable supply. "Non-taxable supply" [Section 2(79)] means a supply of goods or services or both which is not leviable to tax under the CGST Act or the IGST Act.

question_html: As per section 1 of the CGST Act, 2017 and section 1 of the IGST Act, 2017 respectively, the CGST Act and the IGST Act extend to:

options.C: The whole of India, in both cases

question_html: Under the reverse charge mechanism (RCM), as opposed to the normal position where the supplier is liable to pay GST:

options.D: The liability to pay GST is cast on the recipient of the goods or services, and the statutory liability to deposit GST and undertake compliances (registration, deposit, filing returns, etc.) shifts from the supplier to the recipient
options.A: The liability to pay GST is entirely waived for both the supplier and the recipient
options.B: The liability to pay GST is split equally between the supplier and the recipient in every case
options.C: The liability to pay GST shifts to the Electronic Commerce Operator facilitating the transaction, in every RCM case without exception

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) The liability to pay GST is cast on the recipient of the goods or services, and the statutory liability to deposit GST and undertake compliances (registration, deposit, filing returns, etc.) shifts from the supplier to the recipient

Generally, the supplier of goods or services is liable to pay GST. However, under the reverse charge mechanism, the liability to pay GST is cast on the recipient of the goods or services. Under normal circumstances the statutory liability to deposit GST and undertake compliances is on the supplier (though he may recover the same from the recipient); under RCM, this statutory liability shifts from supplier to recipient.

question_html: GTA services are taxable at two alternative rates: 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST/UTGST) where the GTA has not taken ITC on goods/services used in supplying the GTA service, or 18% (9% CGST + 9% SGST/UTGST) where the GTA exercises the option to itself pay GST at that rate. Under which of these two rates does the recipient bear the liability under reverse charge?

options.A: Only under the 5% rate - where GTA has not taken ITC and does not exercise the option to itself pay tax, GST is payable by the recipient under reverse charge; under the 18% rate (GTA exercising the option to itself pay tax), it is always forward charge by the GTA, with no ITC restriction
options.B: Under both the 5% and the 18% rate, the recipient always bears the liability under reverse charge with no exception
options.C: Under the 18% rate only - the 5% rate is always paid under forward charge by the GTA
options.D: Neither - GTA services are entirely exempt from GST regardless of the rate applicable

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Only under the 5% rate - where GTA has not taken ITC and does not exercise the option to itself pay tax, GST is payable by the recipient under reverse charge; under the 18% rate (GTA exercising the option to itself pay tax), it is always forward charge by the GTA, with no ITC restriction

Where the GTA does not exercise the option to itself pay GST (and hence has not taken ITC), GST is payable @ 5% by the recipient under reverse charge (where the recipient is a specified recipient). Where the GTA exercises the option to itself pay GST @ 18% (with no restriction on availing ITC), GST is payable under forward charge by the GTA itself. Where the GTA registers and exercises the forward-charge option at 5% too, that is also forward charge by the GTA.

options.A: The ECO must always itself own and physically deliver the goods or services in question
options.B: The actual supplier is legally irrelevant, since the ECO is treated as the sole supplier of every transaction on its platform for all purposes
options.D: The transaction is automatically outside the scope of GST, since no direct privity of contract exists between the buyer and the ECO

answer_html:
Correct answer: (C) The actual product/service belongs to some other (actual) seller, and the ECO merely collects payment from the customer, deducts its commission, and remits the balance to the actual supplier

Where the ECO connects buyer and seller (the more common model), the actual product/service belongs to some other seller, not the ECO. The customer orders on the app, the actual supplier delivers the product/service, the ECO collects the payment from the customer, deducts its commission and taxes, and remits the balance of the consideration to the actual supplier.

question_html: Under section 9(5) of the CGST Act, the Government has notified specific categories of services (e.g., passenger transportation by radio-taxi/motorcab, hotel accommodation, house-keeping services, restaurant service, and local delivery) supplied through an ECO, where:

options.D: The ECO itself must pay the GST on such notified services (subject to specified exceptions), as if it is the supplier liable for paying the tax, even though the ECO did not itself actually provide the service
options.A: The actual supplier alone remains liable to pay GST in every case, with the ECO bearing no GST liability whatsoever on these services
options.B: GST becomes entirely inapplicable to these categories of services once they are supplied through an ECO
options.C: The customer/recipient of the service becomes liable to pay GST under reverse charge on these notified services

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) The ECO itself must pay the GST on such notified services (subject to specified exceptions), as if it is the supplier liable for paying the tax, even though the ECO did not itself actually provide the service

As per Notification No. 17/2017 CT (R) dated 28.06.2017 (as amended), for specified categories of services (passenger transport by radio-taxi/motorcab/maxicab/motorcycle, hotel/accommodation services, house-keeping services, restaurant service, and local delivery services), the ECO through which such services are supplied is itself liable to pay the GST (subject to specified exceptions), as if it is the supplier liable for paying the tax, even though the actual service was rendered by someone else.

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: Sudheer orders food worth ₹500 from a restaurant through Zomiggy, an ECO. Since restaurant services supplied through an ECO are covered under section 9(5), Zomiggy collects ₹525 (₹500 + ₹25 GST @ 5%) from Sudheer. Who is liable to remit this ₹25 of GST to the Government?

options.A: Zomiggy (the ECO) - since restaurant service is a section 9(5) notified service, the ECO itself remits the GST collected on the food value to the Government, even though the restaurant is the actual supplier of the food
options.B: The restaurant, since it is the actual supplier of the food and Zomiggy is only a facilitator
options.C: Sudheer, the customer, since he is the ultimate consumer who bore the economic burden of the GST
options.D: Neither - restaurant service supplied through an ECO is exempt from GST in every case

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Zomiggy (the ECO) - since restaurant service is a section 9(5) notified service, the ECO itself remits the GST collected on the food value to the Government, even though the restaurant is the actual supplier of the food

Since restaurant services supplied through an ECO are covered under section 9(5), Zomiggy (the ECO) collects the GST on the food value from the customer and remits it to the Government itself - here, the ₹25 GST on the ₹500 food value. Zomiggy separately charges the restaurant a commission plus GST on that commission (which follows the normal forward-charge rule for Zomiggy's own commission services to the restaurant).

question_html: Where an Electronic Commerce Operator liable to pay tax on notified services under section 9(5) does not have a physical presence in the taxable territory, and also does not have a representative in that territory:

options.B: The ECO shall appoint a person in the taxable territory for the purpose of paying tax, and such appointed person shall be liable to pay the tax
options.A: The tax liability is entirely waived, since the ECO cannot be compelled to comply with Indian GST law
options.C: The actual supplier of the underlying service automatically becomes solely liable to pay GST in every such case
options.D: The recipient/customer becomes liable to pay the tax directly to the Government under reverse charge in every such case

answer_html:
Correct answer: (B) The ECO shall appoint a person in the taxable territory for the purpose of paying tax, and such appointed person shall be liable to pay the tax

Where an ECO liable to pay tax under section 9(5) does not have a physical presence in the taxable territory, any person representing such ECO in the taxable territory shall be liable to pay tax. Where the ECO has neither a physical presence nor a representative in the taxable territory, the ECO shall appoint a person in the taxable territory for the purpose of paying tax, and such person shall be liable to pay the tax.

question_html: As clarified by CBIC, is an ECO required to reverse proportionate input tax credit (ITC) on its own input goods/services on account of paying GST on restaurant services under section 9(5)?

options.D: No - ECO shall not be required to reverse ITC on account of restaurant services on which it pays GST under section 9(5); however, on restaurant service, the ECO must pay the entire GST liability in cash, since no ITC can be utilised for payment of GST on restaurant service supplied through the ECO

options.B: No, and the ECO may additionally utilise its accumulated ITC to discharge the GST liability on restaurant service in cash-equivalent proportion

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) No - ECO shall not be required to reverse ITC on account of restaurant services on which it pays GST under section 9(5); however, on restaurant service, the ECO must pay the entire GST liability in cash, since no ITC can be utilised for payment of GST on restaurant service supplied through the ECO

It is clarified that the ECO shall not be required to reverse ITC on account of restaurant services on which it pays GST in terms of section 9(5) - the ITC remains available to the ECO as before, for use in respect of its own services. question_html: Where restaurant service is supplied through an ECO (with the ECO paying GST on it under section 9(5)), is the value of such restaurant service included in the aggregate turnover of the restaurant (the actual supplier of the food)?

question_html: Classification of goods under GST is based on HSN, which stands for "Harmonized System of Nomenclature" - a multipurpose international product nomenclature developed by:

options.B: The World Customs Organization (WCO), comprising about 5,000 commodity groups each identified by a 6-digit code, with India having extended the HSN codes up to 8 digits
options.A: The World Trade Organization (WTO), comprising exactly 1,000 commodity groups identified by a 4-digit code
options.C: The Goods and Services Tax Council of India, exclusively for domestic GST classification purposes
options.D: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), for the specific purpose of examination classification

answer_html:
Correct answer: (B) The World Customs Organization (WCO), comprising about 5,000 commodity groups each identified by a 6-digit code, with India having extended the HSN codes up to 8 digits

HSN (Harmonized System of Nomenclature) is a multipurpose international product nomenclature developed by the World Customs Organization (WCO) for classifying goods across the world in a systematic manner. It comprises about 5,000 commodity groups, each identified by a 6-digit code (which can be extended), and India has extended the HSN codes up to 8 digits.

options.D: Various sections, headings and groups, with further division in the form of Tariff item/Service Code

options.B: 6% (CGST + SGST/UTGST) of turnover for manufacturers, and 1% for restaurant service providers

question_html: Which combination of taxes is applicable to Sanchit Home Décor's two furnishings transactions - (i) the ₹12,00,000 intra-Karnataka supply, and (ii) the ₹9,00,000 supply to Tamil Nadu?

case_facts_html: Sanchit Home Décor Pvt. Ltd. undertakes the following transactions in a month: (i) it supplies decorative furnishings within Karnataka (its own State of registration) to a local retailer for ₹12,00,000, in the ordinary course of its regular (non-composition) business; (ii) it separately supplies similar furnishings to a retailer located in Tamil Nadu for ₹9,00,000; and (iii) it wants to determine the correct GST rate and classification basis applicable to a new range of decorative products it is about to launch.
question_html: Regardless of the actual notified rate ultimately applicable to Sanchit Home Décor's products, what are the maximum statutory rate ceilings that the Government could notify for CGST (on the intra-Karnataka transaction) and IGST (on the Karnataka-to-Tamil-Nadu transaction) respectively?

options.D: 20% for CGST under section 9(1) (with an equivalent SGST rate also applicable, mirroring the CGST rate), and 40% for IGST under section 5(1) of the IGST Act (since IGST is the sum total of CGST and SGST/UTGST)
options.A: 40% for CGST and 20% for IGST - the reverse of the correct statutory ceilings
options.B: 18% for both CGST and IGST, being the standard GST rate applicable to most goods and services
options.C: There is no statutory ceiling on either CGST or IGST; the Government may notify any rate at its discretion

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) 20% for CGST under section 9(1) (with an equivalent SGST rate also applicable, mirroring the CGST rate), and 40% for IGST under section 5(1) of the IGST Act (since IGST is the sum total of CGST and SGST/UTGST)

As per section 9(1) of the CGST Act, the maximum rate of CGST that may be notified is 20% (with SGST/UTGST separately leviable, generally at an equivalent rate). As per section 5(1) of the IGST Act, the maximum rate of IGST is 40%, since IGST is designed as the sum total of CGST and SGST/UTGST.
